one Complex numbers.
In one breath.
A complex number combines real and imaginary components. The same algebra that solves quadratics also unlocks higher degree polynomials when you use conjugate pairs.
Key ideas.

A complex number is z equals a plus i b, where a, b is in the real numbers and i squared equals minus one. Its real part is a and its imaginary part is b, not i b. Two complex numbers are equal only when their real parts match and their imaginary parts match. The conjugate is z star equals a minus i b. The modulus is the modulus of z equals the square root of a squared plus b squared, end root, its distance from the origin. The argument theta is the angle from the positive real axis to the line from the origin to z. Thus a equals r cosine theta, b equals r sine theta, and z equals r cosine theta plus i r sine theta, where r equals the modulus of z.

Plot a plus i b at open bracket a, b close bracket on an Argand diagram, the horizontal axis is real and the vertical axis is imaginary. Addition is vector addition. Multiplying by i rotates a point ninety degrees anticlockwise about the origin. More generally, multiplication combines scaling and rotation, division reverses the denominator's scaling and rotation. In particular, the modulus of, z one z two, end modulus, equals the modulus of z one the modulus of z two and, for z two is not equal to zero, the modulus of, z one over z two, end modulus, equals the modulus of z one over the modulus of z two.

Multiplication by i takes z equals one plus i to i z equals minus one plus i through an anticlockwise quarter turn. The dashed sides complete the parallelogram, whose resultant is z plus i z equals two i. Division by i gives the inverse, clockwise quarter turn, neither operation changes the modulus.
